<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Fix cancelled-job alert visibility">
Fix accepted HIGH issue 7df52070-dc5a-49fc-b3ac-925cecce6f3d in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm (story 843): cancelling a job removes it from Scheduling.list_jobs, so it vanishes from the /schedule board — the office loses ack-status visibility for its schedule-change notification, and escalation (computed read-time in Notifications.latest_schedule_change_for_job, invoked per board-rendered job) can never fire for it: the notification sits "pending" forever.

You own lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling.ex, lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/index.ex, and lib/cleaner_crm/notifications.ex (read paths only) — nothing else.

MCP note: on "No session_id available" add explicit session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8"; if MCP hangs >2 min, message me and keep coding.

Fix approach (adjust if the code suggests better): the board should continue showing a cancelled job — visually distinct (e.g. "Cancelled" badge, muted card, keep [data-test='job-<id>'] and ack-status/channel selectors) — for as long as its latest schedule_change notification is unacknowledged; once acknowledged, it can drop off. That restores office visibility AND lets the existing read-time escalation logic fire naturally. Either extend the board's query (list_jobs opts to include cancelled-with-pending-alerts) or fetch that subset separately in Index — keep Scheduling.list_jobs' default behavior unchanged for other callers (FieldLive must NOT show cancelled jobs to cleaners except via their alert).

Existing specs must stay green — run FULL mix spex (100/100) + mix test (160+/0) + targeted mix spex 843_*/ 833_*/ 834_*/; mix format. NO dev compile/server restart — say "NEEDS RELEASE REBUILD". resolve_issue when green. Final response: files, counts, notes. Under 120 words.

3	  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
4	  conflict-aware assignment.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
7	  """
8	
9	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
10	
11	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

28	
29	  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    Job
31	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
32	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
33	    |> Repo.get!(id)
34	  end
35	
36	  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
37	    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
38	  end
39	
40	  @doc """
41	  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
42	  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
43	  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
44	  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
45	  """
46	  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
47	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
48	    with {:ok, job} <-
49	           %Job{account_id: account_id}
50	           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
51	           |> Repo.insert() do
52	      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
53	      {:ok, job}
54	    end
55	  end
56	
57	  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
58	  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
59	  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
60	  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
61	  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
62	  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
63	  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
64	  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
65	  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
66	  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
67	  # left alone.
68	  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
69	    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
70	      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
71	        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
72	        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
73	      end
74	    else
75	      attrs
76	    end
77	  end
78	
79	  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
80	    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
81	      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
82	        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
83	        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
84	        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
85	          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
86	        else
87	          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
88	        end
89	
90	      _ ->
91	        attrs
92	    end
93	  end
94	
95	  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))
96	
97	  defp blank?(nil), do: true
98	  defp blank?(""), do: true
99	  defp blank?(_value), do: false
100	
101	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
102	    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
103	  end
104	
105	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
106	    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
107	  end
108	
109	  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
110	  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
111	  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
112	  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable

114	  defp job_created_values(job) do
115	    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
116	  end

118	  @doc """
119	  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
120	  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
121	  """

123	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
124	    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

126	    Job
127	    |> where(

131	    )
132	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
133	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
134	    |> Repo.all()
135	  end

137	  @doc """
138	  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
139	  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
140	  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
141	  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.

145	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)

149	  end

152	  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
153	  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
154	  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
155	  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
156	  """

159	    with :ok <-
160	           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(

162	             cleaner_id,
163	             job.scheduled_date,
164	             job.start_time,
165	             job.end_time,

167	           ),

169	      Recorder.record(
170	        scope,
171	        "job_reassigned",
172	        "Job",
173	        updated.id,
174	        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
175	        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
176	      )
177	
178	      {:ok, updated}
179	    end
180	  end

183	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
184	    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
185	      Recorder.record(
186	        scope,
187	        "job_cancelled",
188	        "Job",
189	        updated.id,
190	        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
191	        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
192	      )
193	
194	      {:ok, updated}
195	    end
196	  end

202	  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
203	  """

205	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
206	    changeset = Job.changeset(job, derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
207	
208	    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
209	      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
210	      {:ok, updated}
211	    end
212	  end

215	
216	  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
217	    changed_fields =
218	      changeset.changes
219	      |> Map.keys()
220	      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))
221	
222	    if changed_fields != [] do
223	      Recorder.record(
224	        scope,
225	        update_action(changed_fields),

227	        updated.id,
228	        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),

236	      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
237	        "job_rescheduled"
238	
239	      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
  # left alone.
  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
      end
    else
      attrs
    end
  end

  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
        else
          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
        end

      _ ->
        attrs
    end
  end

  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))

  defp blank?(nil), do: true
  defp blank?(""), do: true
  defp blank?(_value), do: false

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """
  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single cleaner by id, for their detail page. Draws from
  the same membership list as `list_cleaners/1`, so a user who isn't
  a member of this account can't be looked up here either. Raises if
  not found.
  """
  def get_cleaner!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(id)

    scope
    |> list_cleaners()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
    |> case do
      nil -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: User
      cleaner -> cleaner
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's time-off blocks for their detail page, soonest
  first.
  """
  def list_availability_blocks(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where([b], b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id)
    |> order_by([b], asc: b.date)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's upcoming (today or later, non-cancelled) jobs for
  their detail page, soonest first.
  """
  def list_upcoming_jobs_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.status != :cancelled and j.scheduled_date >= ^Date.utc_today()
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id
  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id)

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
4	  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
5	  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
6	  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.
7	
8	  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
9	  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
10	  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
11	  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
12	  """
13	
14	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
15	
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
17	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
18	
19	  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{

96	    Notification
97	    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
98	    |> Repo.exists?()
99	  end

102	  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
103	    Notification
104	    |> where(
105	      [n],
106	      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
107	    )

112	  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
113	  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the

125	  end

128	
129	  @doc """
130	  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
131	  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
132	  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
133	  """

135	      when is_binary(sid) do

137	    # inserts (or duplicated test data) must not 500 the endpoint.

139	      from(n in Notification,
140	        where: n.provider_message_id == ^sid,

153

155	    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
156	  end
157

159	       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do

162	      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
  end

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification,
        status: :reschedule_requested,
        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      )
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
    )
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc """
  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
  `:reschedule_requested`.
  """
  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([n], n.status)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    # Most-recent match: real SIDs are unique, but webhook retries racing
    # inserts (or duplicated test data) must not 500 the endpoint.
    notification =
      from(n in Notification,
        where: n.provider_message_id == ^sid,
        order_by: [desc: n.inserted_at],
        limit: 1
      )
      |> Repo.one()

    case notification do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(
         %Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification
       )
       when not is_nil(client_id) do
    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
    token = generate_token()

    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending
    )
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
  ack status on the board.
  """
  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
    )
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
    |> maybe_escalate()
  end

  # A same-day change nobody has acknowledged within the escalation
  # window re-sends via the fallback channel (SMS) and flags as
  # escalated for office visibility. Computed on read rather than a
  # separate periodic pass — every read of a job's alert (the board,
  # `FieldLive.Today`) goes through here, so none of them can show a
  # stale "pending" past the window.
  @escalation_window_seconds 600

  defp maybe_escalate(%Notification{status: :pending} = notification) do
    if escalation_due?(notification) do
      {:ok, updated} =
        update_status(notification,
          status: :escalated,
          channel: :sms,
          escalated_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        )

      updated
    else
      notification
    end
  end

  defp maybe_escalate(notification), do: notification

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: nil}), do: false

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: pushed_at, job_id: job_id}) do
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, job_id)

    Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :gt and
      DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), pushed_at, :second) >= @escalation_window_seconds
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

## Cancelled job's schedule-change notification is invisible to the office and can never escalate (ID: 7df52070-dc5a-49fc-b3ac-925cecce6f3d)

**Severity:** high | **Scope:** app | **Status:** accepted | **Story:** 843

Reproduction: as owner on /schedule, cancel a cleaner's job via [data-test='job-<id>-cancel-button']. A schedule_change notification (kind=schedule_change, status=pending, channel=push, summary="Cancelled") is correctly created and the cleaner sees the "Cancelled" alert on /field (confirmed via psql + browser).

However, `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.list_jobs/1` (lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling.ex:143) filters `where j.status != :cancelled`, so a cancelled job's row (and its `[data-test='job-<id>-ack-status']` / `[data-test='job-<id>-notification-channel']` indicators) disappears from ScheduleLive.Index entirely the moment it's cancelled.

Two consequences, both against story 843's acceptance criteria:
1. "Office sees who has not acknowledged" fails specifically for cancellations: there is no way for the office to see whether the cleaner has acknowledged a job cancellation, since the board never renders that job's row again.
2. "Never-acknowledged same-day change escalates" never fires for cancellations: `CleanerCrm.Notifications.maybe_escalate/1` (lib/cleaner_crm/notifications.ex) — the function that flips a stale pending notification to :escalated and re-sends via SMS — is only invoked from `latest_schedule_change_for_job/2`, which is only ever called by ScheduleLive.Index.schedule_change_alert/2 for jobs in `@jobs`. Since cancelled jobs are excluded from that list, a cancellation notification can sit `pending` forever with no escalation check ever running, no matter how long it goes unacknowledged.

This is arguably the highest-stakes case for the whole story: a cleaner who never sees/acknowledges that their job was cancelled might show up anyway, and the office has no way to notice the unacknowledged cancellation because the row is gone.

Expected: the office should still be able to see acknowledgment status (and escalation) for a cancelled job's schedule-change notification, e.g. by not filtering cancelled jobs out of the board (or showing them in a distinct "cancelled" section) at least while they carry an unacknowledged/escalated notification.

Verified via: browser session as qa-owner/qa-cleaner, job dbd5a7b7-5390-423f-9fab-ca100cdcced8, and psql confirming the notification row (id 5dd646b7-e1d6-450b-9734-a2395e66cd2a) stays status=pending indefinitely with no escalation path reachable.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]

    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
  end

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification,
        status: :reschedule_requested,
        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      )
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
    )
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc """
  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
  `:reschedule_requested`.
  """
  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([n], n.status)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    # Most-recent match: real SIDs are unique, but webhook retries racing
    # inserts (or duplicated test data) must not 500 the endpoint.
    notification =
      from(n in Notification,
        where: n.provider_message_id == ^sid,
        order_by: [desc: n.inserted_at],
        limit: 1
      )
      |> Repo.one()

    case notification do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(
         %Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification
       )
       when not is_nil(client_id) do
    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
    token = generate_token()

    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending
    )
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
  ack status on the board.
  """
  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
    )
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
    |> maybe_escalate()
  end

  # A same-day change nobody has acknowledged within the escalation
  # window re-sends via the fallback channel (SMS) and flags as
  # escalated for office visibility. Computed on read rather than a
  # separate periodic pass — every read of a job's alert (the board,
  # `FieldLive.Today`) goes through here, so none of them can show a
  # stale "pending" past the window.
  @escalation_window_seconds 600

  defp maybe_escalate(%Notification{status: :pending} = notification) do
    if escalation_due?(notification) do
      {:ok, updated} =
        update_status(notification,
          status: :escalated,
          channel: :sms,
          escalated_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        )

      updated
    else
      notification
    end
  end

  defp maybe_escalate(notification), do: notification

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: nil}), do: false

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: pushed_at, job_id: job_id}) do
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, job_id)

    Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :gt and
      DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), pushed_at, :second) >= @escalation_window_seconds
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow

    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)

    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)
